description: A developer joins a new team to work on an existing mid-size web project. They need to learn about the code repository, dev environment, and team roles.

user_profile.context: First day on the new project team, needs to ramp up quickly

fact_sheet.fact: Anya Sharma is the Tech Lead for Project Phoenix.
Ben Carter is the Senior Backend Engineer and your assigned onboarding buddy.
The team's primary Slack channel for project communication is #proj-phoenix.
Carlos Diaz is the primary DevOps contact; his Slack handle is @carlos.diaz.
Dana White is the Product Manager for Project Phoenix.
The daily stand-up meeting is at 9:15 AM PST via the Google Meet link meet.google.com/abc-xyz-pqr.
The team operates on a 2-week sprint cycle, starting on Mondays.
All development tasks are tracked as tickets in Jira under the project key 'PHX'.
The active sprint board is located at innovatech.atlassian.net/jira/software/projects/PHX/boards/123.
Pull Requests (PRs) to the 'develop' branch require a minimum of two approvals from team members.
One of the two required PR approvals must be from a senior developer: Anya Sharma or Ben Carter.
The project's primary code repository is hosted on GitHub Enterprise at github.innovatech.com/phoenix/phoenix-web-app.
The main development branch is named 'develop'; feature branches must be created from this branch.
The backend is a monolithic application written in Python 3.11 using the Django 4.2 framework.
The frontend is a Single Page Application (SPA) built with React 18 and TypeScript 5.1.
The repository uses a pre-commit hook to enforce the Conventional Commits v1.0.0 specification.
The local development environment is managed entirely through Docker and Docker Compose.
To build and start the local environment, run the command 'docker-compose up --build -d' from the project root directory.
The team's standard Integrated Development Environment (IDE) is JetBrains PyCharm Professional 2023.2.
A license for PyCharm can be requested by filing an IT ticket in Jira under the 'ITSUP' project.
The Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment (CI/CD) pipeline is managed by Jenkins, accessible at ci.innovatech.internal.
Backend Python dependencies are managed using Poetry 1.5.
The staging environment is deployed automatically upon every successful merge to the 'develop' branch.
The URL for the staging environment is https://staging.phoenix-app.io.
The local development database is a PostgreSQL 15 instance running in a dedicated Docker container.
The production environment is hosted on Amazon Web Services (AWS) in the us-west-2 (Oregon) region.
Read-only access credentials for the staging database can be found in the 1Password 'Phoenix-Staging' vault.
The project's primary documentation and knowledge base is in Confluence at innovatech.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/PHX.
A link to the 'New Developer Setup Guide' is pinned in the #proj-phoenix Slack channel.
The REST API documentation is generated via Swagger and is browsable on the staging environment at https://staging.phoenix-app.io/api/v1/docs.
Architectural Decision Records (ADRs) are maintained in Markdown format within the '/docs/adr' directory of the main code repository.
Sprint planning meetings occur every other Monday at 10:00 AM PST.
Code is deployed to production every Thursday at 2:00 PM PST, following a successful staging verification.

user_needs.description: Where is the project's main code repository hosted?
What is the command to build and start the local development environment?
user_needs.prediction_reason: Intra-group: After finding the code repository, the immediate next step for a hands-on developer is to get the environment running locally.

user_needs.description: Who is the Tech Lead and who is my assigned onboarding buddy?
What is the team's primary Slack channel for project communication?
user_needs.prediction_reason: Intra-group: After identifying key team members, the user will want to know the primary channel to communicate with them and the rest of the team.

user_needs.description: Where are development tasks tracked and what is the link to the active sprint board?
What are the approval requirements for pull requests to the 'develop' branch?
user_needs.prediction_reason: Intra-group: Once the user knows where to find tasks, they will need to understand the process for submitting the resulting code for review and merging.

user_needs.description: Where can I find the new developer setup guide?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After the user asks how to start the local environment, it's helpful to proactively offer a link to the comprehensive setup guide for further details.

user_needs.description: What time is the daily stand-up meeting and what is the meeting link?
What are the primary frameworks and languages used for the backend and frontend?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: After getting the location of the codebase, a developer is likely to be curious about the tech stack they will be working with.

user_needs.description: What is the URL for the staging environment?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: Understanding the PR approval process naturally leads to questions about the subsequent steps in the pipeline, such as where to view the changes in a deployed environment.

user_needs.description: Who is the primary DevOps contact?
user_needs.prediction_reason: CROSS-GROUP: While discussing the local Docker-based environment setup, it's a relevant and helpful time to proactively mention who to contact for DevOps or infrastructure-related issues.
